places.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
places.description: One of the most sacred Hindu temples in India, dedicated to Lord Shiva as Vishwanath (Lord of the Universe). The current temple was built in 1780 by Ahilyabai Holkar; the two spires were gold-plated under Ranjit Singh in 1835. Entry restricted to Hindus and those of verifiable Hindu faith; the new Kashi Vishwanath Corridor (2021) has transformed access significantly. Dawn and early morning darshan recommended.

places.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
places.description: Varanasi's most prominent and busiest ghat on the Ganges, where evening Ganga Aarti is performed nightly by brahmin priests with fire and incense. The ceremony begins around sunset and draws hundreds of worshippers and tourists. Morning boat rides departing from this ghat offer the classic Varanasi sunrise experience. No entry fee; boat rides charged separately.
places.openingDays: Open all day; Aarti nightly at sunset (~18:30–19:30 seasonally)

places.name: Manikarnika Ghat
places.description: The primary cremation ghat of Varanasi, considered the most auspicious place to die and be cremated in Hinduism. Funeral pyres burn around the clock; Hindus bring their dead from across India. Photography is strictly prohibited out of respect. Visitors may observe from a respectful distance from boats or the ghat steps. A genuinely sacred and sobering site.

places.name: Assi Ghat
places.description: Southernmost major ghat at the confluence of the Assi and Ganges rivers, less crowded than Dashashwamedh. A favourite gathering point for students, sadhus and foreigners; morning yoga sessions held on the steps. The narrow lanes behind the ghat have cafes and bookshops popular with long-stay travellers. Good sunrise point.

places.name: Sarnath
places.description: Site of the Buddha's first sermon after Enlightenment (Dharmachakra), 13km north of Varanasi. The Dhamek Stupa (500 CE) and ruins of the ancient Nalanda-era monastery complex are UNESCO-protected. The Sarnath Museum holds the Lion Capital of Ashoka (India's national emblem) and superb Gupta-period Buddhist sculpture. A half-day excursion from Varanasi.

places.name: Gyanvapi Mosque
places.description: 17th-century mosque built by Aurangzeb adjacent to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, widely regarded as having been constructed over an earlier Shiva temple. The minaret of the earlier structure remains visible. A historically contested and politically sensitive site; approach with respect. Access may be restricted.
places.openingDays: Open to Muslim worshippers; visitor access may be restricted

places.name: Ramnagar Fort
places.description: 18th-century fort and palace on the east bank of the Ganges, 14km from central Varanasi by road, residence of the Maharaja of Banaras. The Ramnagar Fort Museum holds vintage cars, ivory artefacts, howdahs and Mughal armaments. Cross by the Rajghat Bridge or boat. The fort is most famous for the month-long Ramlila performance held in the surrounding town each autumn.

places.name: Munshi Ghat
places.description: Quieter residential ghat flanked by a crumbling haveli palace and the typical layered facades of Varanasi's riverfront. Particularly photogenic at sunrise when the light catches the peeling ochre and ochre plaster. Far less crowded than Dashashwamedh; a good base for extended ghat exploration.

places.name: Jantar Mantar Varanasi
places.description: One of five astronomical observatories built by Raja Jai Singh II of Jaipur in the early 18th century, located within the Man Mandir Ghat palace complex. Smaller and less-visited than the Jaipur counterpart. The Man Mandir Ghat itself offers excellent views of the river. Entry via the ghat.

places.name: Bharat Mata Mandir
places.description: Unusual temple dedicated to Mother India (Bharat Mata), inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1936. Instead of religious idols, the inner sanctum houses a large detailed relief map of undivided India carved from marble. A pilgrimage site of secular nationalism rather than religion. Near BHU Cantt station.

places.name: Vishalakshi Temple
places.description: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, marking the site where the earrings of Sati fell. Dedicated to Vishalakshi (large-eyed goddess), an aspect of Parvati. Located in the old city near the main ghat cluster, this ancient temple is an important pilgrimage stop on the Kashi Panchakroshi Yatra.

places.name: Varanasi Street Food — Kachori Sabzi
places.description: Banarasi breakfast staple: deep-fried lentil kachori served with tangy aloo sabzi and a tamarind chutney. Famous spots near Dashashwamedh Ghat and Godowlia Crossing. Paired with a cup of thick malai chai.

places.name: Thandai and Bhang Lassi Experience
places.description: Varanasi's iconic thandai (chilled milk drink with almonds and spices) from Blue Lassi shop or Government Bhang Shop near Maidagin. Bhang lassi is a traditional cannabis-infused drink legal in certain licensed shops. Integral to Holi and Shivratri culture.

places.name: Ganga Funsion Rooftop Dining
places.description: Several rooftop restaurants overlooking the Ganga ghats offer a contemplative dining experience — watching cremations at Manikarnika and the river from above while eating Banarasi thali. Prices vary; independent travellers favour Aum Restaurant and Brown Bread Bakery.
